title: The permission that survived revocation
blurb: Delete-after-write cache invalidation resurrected revoked grants.
prompt: A removed contractor kept access for twenty minutes because a concurrent read repopulated the permission cache after the draft deleted it. The same service failed open on policy-engine timeouts and let team admins grant org-wide roles. Review it, fix it, and prove revocation is immediate and grants cannot escalate.
aiNote: The draft invalidates the cache by deleting keys after a grant change, so a racing read can re-derive and store the pre-change set, and it falls back to cached allow when the policy engine times out, turning an outage into broad access.
testIdea: Revoke a permission and immediately call the same check on another connection and assert denial; time out the policy engine and assert denial; attempt a grant exceeding the assigner's permissions and assert 403.
followUps: What does fail closed cost during a policy outage?
How do you audit who could grant what?
Should effective permissions ever be cached client-side?
